text: dsh-web-search-anysearch 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的网页搜索提供器：它注册到 ctx.web，并通过 AnySearch 的 JSON-RPC 接口承接 web_search。插件将搜索结果解析为带标题、网址和摘要的引用来源，支持按领域筛选、结果数量与超时配置，并在响应格式变化时保留原始内容供模型使用。它也提供插件设置页管理可选 API 密钥。适合需要让 DSH 模型联网检索资料的用户；匿名搜索即可使用，密钥可提高额度。

dsh-web-search-anysearch connects DSH web_search to AnySearch. It registers through ctx.web, sends searches over JSON-RPC, and turns results into citeable titles, links, and snippets. Users can set a search domain and result limit. Anonymous access works; an optional key provides higher limits.
想让 DSH 的网页搜索改用 AnySearch。
有没有办法让 DSH 根据问题联网找网页资料？
希望搜索结果带上标题、链接和摘要，方便模型引用。
我想把搜索限定在学术或金融等领域。
匿名搜索额度不够时，怎样给 DSH 配置搜索服务密钥？
DSH 搜索服务返回的格式变化时，仍想把原始结果交给模型。
Route DSH web searches through the AnySearch API.
Let my DSH agent search the web and return citeable links.
dsh-web-search-anysearch 的功能「网页搜索提供器」：在 DSH 调用 web_search 时通过 AnySearch 执行 search 请求，并将查询、结果数和可选领域传给服务。
dsh-web-search-anysearch 的功能「解析引用来源」：将 AnySearch 的 Markdown 搜索结果整理为标题、网址和摘要；重复网址只保留首次出现的结果。
dsh-web-search-anysearch 的功能「领域筛选」：可配置 general、academic、finance、code 等搜索领域；非 general 领域会随搜索请求发送。
dsh-web-search-anysearch 的功能「密钥设置页」：网页插件设置页可查看密钥是否已配置、写入或清除凭据；密钥通过 credentials 服务管理。
dsh-web-search-anysearch 使用 AnySearch 的 api.anysearch.com 服务执行搜索并发送查询；匿名访问可用，API 密钥仅用于提高额度。 (见 src/provider.ts:98-117)
dsh-web-search-anysearch 的设置页通过 DSH credentials 服务保存或清除密钥引用；代码说明该密钥不会写入插件配置文件。 (见 src/client.ts:10-17)

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · dsh-web-search-anysearch：A [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that
provides web search through [AnySearch](https://anysearch.com) — "AI Search Infrastructure
for Agents".

**Requires dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.2** — this plugin targets the dsh RC/stable line only (CI and releases resolve the newest of the `latest`/`next` dist-tags at runtime). **The alpha line is no longer supported.**

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · dsh-web-search-anysearch：The plugin registers a `WebSearchProvider` (`id: "anysearch"`) with the official
[`ctx.web` capability seam](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/main/packages/web/web),
so the model keeps calling the same `web_search` tool with the same citation formatting
and bounds. No third-party SDK is used: the transport follows AnySearch's own reference
CLI ([anysearch-ai/anysearch-skill](https://github.com/anysearch-ai/anysearch-skill)).
@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · How it talks to AnySearch：Per the official interface spec (`scripts/shared/doc_spec.md` in the skill repo):

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · How it talks to AnySearch：- `POST https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` — JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call`, **stateless** (no
  `initialize`, no session, one connection per request).
- `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` is **optional** — anonymous access works with lower
  rate limits. A free key is available at [anysearch.com/console/api-keys](https://anysearch.com/console/api-keys).
- `max_results` is capped at 10 by the API.
- Responses are *structured Markdown for agents*; the provider parses result blocks into
  citeable sources, and degrades to passing the whole payload through as `content` if the
  format ever drifts — a search never fails just because the parser did.
- Raw `node:https` per request (not `fetch`/undici), matching the official CLI and
  avoiding a known undici connection-pool hang on this endpoint.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · How it talks to AnySearch：Vertical routing (`domain`/`sub_domain` via `get_sub_domains`), `batch_search`, and
`extract` remain richer MCP/skill-layer features; this provider deliberately exposes the
general `search` tool to dsh's model-facing `web_search` (a `domain` can be pinned in
config). Point an MCP client at AnySearch for the full toolset.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Install：One command:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch
```

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Install：`dsh plugin` installs the package into the profile (via pnpm) and registers it in
`dsh.profile.bundles` automatically — the package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the
official CLI reconciles the layer stack by itself. Restart dsh. **That is the whole
install**: the plugin mounts itself AND claims the `web_search` default at the bundle
layer, so with zero configuration the model's `web_search` tool runs on AnySearch
(anonymous access needs no key).

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Install：Local development: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add link:/path/to/dsh-web-search-anysearch`
(relative path specs anchor to your invoking directory). The manual route — adding the
dependency and the bundle entry to `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/package.json` yourself and
running `pnpm install` there — works identically.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove @aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch
```

The host auto-cleans the whole install: the bundles entry is spliced out of the
profile's `package.json`, the dependency is removed, and the plugin's patch
layer drops with the package — **including the `searchProvider: anysearch`
claim** the patch placed on the host `web` row, so `web_search` reverts to the
host default (`deepseek-official`). Restart dsh and it is as if the plugin was
never installed.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Uninstall：One caveat: if you hand-copied the selection into your **own** patch layer
(`searchProvider: anysearch` in the profile or home `cordis.patch.yml`), that
line outlives the plugin — searches then fail gracefully with
`WEB_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (no provider with that id is registered) until you
delete the line.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Configure (all optional)：**API key — only needed for higher rate limits.** Anonymous access is valid AnySearch
usage; when the anonymous quota runs out, the search error names the credential to
configure. Store the key in dsh's managed credentials document
(`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`):

```yaml
version: 1
refs:
  ANYSEARCH_API_KEY: <your_key>
```

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Configure (all optional)：Or fill it from the GUI: **Settings → Plugins → the `dsh-web-search-anysearch` bundle →
its `web-search-anysearch` row → Configure**. That page writes the reference the
row's own configuration names — `apiKeyEnv`, or `ANYSEARCH_API_KEY` when config
names none — through dsh's credentials service and reports whether a key is
currently configured. Because that field is live, re-pointing `apiKeyEnv` moves
the page and the provider together instead of splitting them — a settings write
applies to the next search, a patch edit at the next start — and a key staged on
the page is dropped if the reference changes under it. The field is
write-only — a stored key never rides a response back to the page — and a blank
field keeps the current key. One more click
(**Clear key**, which asks once) removes the reference again, returning searches to the
anonymous limits. A key supplied by the launching environment or a `.env` fallback is
read-only, and the page says so instead of offering a write.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Configure (all optional)：Both routes land in the same document under the same reference, so they are
interchangeable: a key typed in the GUI is visible to a hand edit and vice versa.
Nothing is written into a configuration file, and the provider re-resolves the
reference on every search, so no restart is needed either way.

**Keep another engine as the default?** Your own patch layer always outranks the
plugin's bundle patch — one entry, no need to touch the plugin:

```yaml

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · profile cordis.patch.yml or ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml：- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: tavily   # or deepseek-official, exa, ...
```

**Verify** which engine owns `web_search`:

```sh
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config | grep -A3 'id: web$'
```

**Plugin config** (all optional; via a patch layer, read at startup):

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · profile cordis.patch.yml or ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml：| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKeyEnv` | `ANYSEARCH_API_KEY` | Credential reference resolved per search. Live: the GUI row reads the accepted value and manages that same reference; a blank value names none, so both halves use the default |
| `apiKey` | — | Literal key; wins over the reference |
| `endpoint` | `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` | Env override: `ANYSEARCH_ENDPOINT` |
| `timeoutMs` | `30000` | Per-request budget |
| `domain` | — (general) | Pin a vertical: `finance`, `academic`, `code`, … (17 total) |
| `maxResults` | `8` | Default when the tool sends no bound; API caps at 10 |

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Behavior：- Markdown result blocks map to sources: `title`, `url`, snippet text; relative
  `date:`/`sitelinks:` annotations stay inside the snippet (no ISO dates → `publishedAt`
  is never set); duplicate URLs dedupe.
- Seam error contract: cancellation as `WEB_ABORTED`; transport failures, non-2xx
  statuses, JSON-RPC errors, and `isError` tool results as `WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` with the
  provider's message surfaced.
- `available()` is a local check only (parseable endpoint) — anonymous access means no
  key is required to be usable.

@aiwayds/dsh-web-search-anysearch README · Develop：The browser half (`src/client.ts` → `lib/client.js`) is a classic script the Web page
evaluates directly, so `npm run build` also runs `scripts/build-client.mjs`: TypeScript
always marks a `.ts` file in this package as a module, and that step strips the marker it
adds and fails the build if the artifact ever carries module syntax. `npm test` covers
the Client half too — artifact shape, the row page it claims, and the credential writes
it performs.
